# Klar til amerikanske regnskaber - endelig tid til tal

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-10-12  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Michael Friis Jørgensen of H.C. Andersen Capital is the in-studio guest. He thinks investors are moving away from AI infrastructure and memory chips, where they question whether the cycle has peaked, and towards European and Danish equities. Ahead of the US bank earnings he expects a positive surprise because the banks have talked expectations down. He and Per Hansen of Nordnet see Danish and Nordic banks, including Nordea, as stable and boring but solid. However, Per thinks further re-rating is limited. Michael sees ASML and TSMC as the safest long-term AI bottleneck plays. Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen calls the Trump–Putin diesel deal negligible and expects Brent to settle at USD 70-90 after the crisis.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟡 NDA-SE — Nordea | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Q3 report Thursday is expected to be stable, with ROE above 15%, a cost ratio of 44-45% and a possible buyback update; Nordic banks are seen as the safest earnings season.

#### Reasoning

Guest Per Hansen (Nordnet) expects Nordea to deliver boring, stable results at the top of the Nordic ROE range, possibly with extra capital returns. Michael says banks are the one place he is 100% sure of very good Danish earnings. However, Per warns the re-rating from below book value is largely done. At about 1.5x book, expected returns roughly equal ROE, so further gains depend on continued strong results.

#### Sell Triggers

- if French/European debt stress hits bank funding
- if rising rates crack the housing market and lift loan losses
- if ROE falls below 15%

> *"de leverer kedeligt stabilt, solidt og de har altså for vane at lægge sig helt i toppen"*

---

### 🟢 JPM — JPMorgan Chase | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 50%

Michael expects a positive post-earnings reaction because the banks have talked down trading and IPO expectations.

#### Reasoning

Michael argues that, unusually, the US banks have not rallied into earnings and have guided expectations lower. That sets up a positive surprise, so he will play them in his stock game. This is a short-term trade, not a fundamental call.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the report shows consumer credit stress
- if trading revenues miss even the lowered expectations

> *"jeg tror faktisk, at de kommer til at reagere positivt"*

---

### 🟢 GS — Goldman Sachs | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Included in Michael's short-term US bank earnings trade.

#### Reasoning

Expectations for trading and IPO activity have been talked down, so Michael sees potential for a positive earnings reaction.

#### Sell Triggers

- if investment banking and trading revenues miss

> *"Vi skal have en masse banker herinde"*

### 🟢 WFC — Wells Fargo | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Included in Michael's short-term US bank earnings trade; the consumer credit read is the key focus.

#### Reasoning

Low expectations set up a positive reaction. The consumer credit read is the main watch point.

#### Sell Triggers

- if consumer credit losses rise

> *"Vi skal have en masse banker herinde"*

---

### 🟢 C — Citigroup | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Included in Michael's short-term US bank earnings trade.

#### Reasoning

Low expectations after warnings on trading and IPOs mean upside potential on earnings day.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit spreads widen sharply

> *"Vi skal have en masse banker herinde"*

---

### 🟡 ASML — ASML | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Near-monopoly and the surest long-term AI bottleneck; holders should stay calm for 10 years, but Michael won't say buy before earnings.

#### Reasoning

Michael holds a small position and calls ASML the world's most brilliant business model and the most certain AI bottleneck over 10 years, with 90% certainty. Valuation is still on the high side, and the earnings reaction depends on a guidance raise and comments on 2027 and China. He advises long-term holders to stay put rather than chase before the report.

#### Sell Triggers

- if guidance isn't raised or 2027 commentary is weak
- if Chinese lithography competition erodes the monopoly
- if China sales fall sharply

> *"Alle dem, der ligger med den, tag det nu roligt over de næste 10 år."*

---

### 🟢 TSM — TSMC | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Michael sees an 80% probability it's a good long-term bottleneck play whatever chip type wins; rising capex would lift the sector.

#### Reasoning

TSMC produces and packages whichever chip becomes the bottleneck (GPU, CPU or memory), so Michael sees it as a safer AI play than memory. He dismisses the Taiwan invasion risk premium. Sales are up about 50%, so gross margin and capex budgets are the focus. A capex increase would signal a strong 2027 for the chip sector.

#### Sell Triggers

- if capex budgets are cut
- if gross margin disappoints
- if a geopolitical escalation over Taiwan happens

> *"TSMC er jo med 80% sandsynlighed et godt sted at spille en langsigtet flaskehals"*

---

### 🟠 MU — Micron | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Michael is nervous memory chips are 'as good as it gets': cheap on P/E, but cyclical, and Chinese capacity (CXMT) is coming.

#### Reasoning

Memory makers show about 60% growth and a P/E below the market, but Michael compares them to shipping at its 2006-07 peak. Chinese capacity and possibly less memory-hungry AI models could end the bottleneck. Returns would be large if the peak has not come, but he prefers safer bottlenecks.

#### Sell Triggers

- if memory prices roll over
- if new AI models need less memory
- if Chinese capacity floods the market

> *"Det er jo derfor, at jeg er lidt nervøs for hukommelseschips."*
